CITY OF READING, OHIO 
COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES – LEGISLATIVE SESSION 
July 7 , 202 6 – 7:30 PM 
For the full detail of this evening’s Council Meeting, please visit www.watchreadingohio.com . 
Opening and Roll Call 
The meeting was called to order at 7:30pm by President Mattscheck with an invocation and the Pledge of Allegiance. 
Council members present: Mr. Powell, Mr. Bronner, Mr. Bishop, Mr. B oe hner, Mr. T ha mann, and Mrs. Eadicicco . 
Mrs. Kro e ger was absent. Motion was made by Mr. Powell, seconded by Mr. Bronner to excuse Mrs. Kro e ger. 
Motion carried by 6 - 0 voice vote. 
Other city officials in attendance included Law Director Mr. Stevenson, Mayor Mr. Bem me s, and Treasurer Mrs. 
Owens . 
Minutes for Approval 
Minutes of the June 2, 2026 and June 16, 2026 Council Meetings were approved. Motion by Mr. Bish op, second by 
Mr. Boehner. Motion carried by 6 - 0 voice vote. 
Public Hearing – 2027 Budget 
• President Mattscheck declared the public hearing open for the proposed 2027 City Budget at 7:32pm. 
• Finance C hairman Mr. Bronner summarized the budget, noting: 
o Tax revenues are expected to remain relatively flat in 2026 with modest growth in 2027. 
o State and local government revenues were conservatively budgeted. 
o Charges for services, permits and fines are expected to increase slightly. 
o General Fund revenues for 2027 are budgeted at approximately $11.74 million, exceeding projected 
expenditures. 
o The Street Maintenance Fund, Capital Improvement Fund, Sewer Service Fee Fund and Fire/EMS 
Capital Improvement Fund remain financially stable. 
o One ambulance purchase is planned for 2027. 
o Recommended transfers include: 
▪ $250,000 from the Earnings Tax Fund to the Growth Fund. 
▪ $200,000 from the Stadium Fund to the General Fund. 
• During public comment, Maggie Wilson requested future funding consideration for accessibility 
improvements, including ADA access to Koenig Park and additional curb cuts around the city. 
• There was no furt her discussion so President Ma ttscheck declared the public hearing closed at 7:37pm. 
Audience Asking Participation

Page 2 07 - 0 7 - 202 6 Reading Council Minutes 
• Bob Wimmers addressed Council regarding the proposed Reading Road R oad diet. He expressed concerns 
about increasing traffic volumes, industrial growth, and questioned whether speed is the primary cause of 
accidents on Reading Road. He also thanked city officials for efforts to attract new industry. Council 
discussed factors identified by ODOT, including speed, lane widths, roadway design, and pedestrian safety 
issues. 
• Mark H aeufle spoke regarding the proposed road diet, raising concerns about traffic backups, turning 
movements, railroad crossings, utility relocations, side - street traffic diversion, emergency access, and 
overall congestion. He urged Council to delay the project pendi ng further study. He also recommended 
increased police presence during scheduled Interstate 75 closures. Council members responded by citing 
ODOT's traffic studies, travel - time analyses, and ongoing willingness to modify designs based on public 
feedback. 
• Maggie Wilson returned to address Council regarding potential traffic diversion onto local streets if the road 
diet proceeds. She expressed concerns about pedestrian safety along Jefferson Avenue and advocated for 
increased traffic enforcement rather than lane reduction s. She also requested to be addressed by her 
preferred name rather than formal titles. Council discussed recent efforts to restore traffic enforcement 
programs and the challenges associated with enforcement staffing and scheduling . 
• Lisa Durbin thanked the City for publishing a community newsletter but requested that future editions 
include information regarding the Reading Road project, police department matters, and contact 
information for city officials. She noted concerns about residents who do not use email or social media . T he 
Mayor and Council responded by outlining the newsletter development process, plans for additional 
newsletters, and ways residents may contact elected officials. 
• Sue Rinderle questioned the effectiveness and publicity of public surveys regarding the Reading Road 
project and asked whether businesses along Reading Road had been consulted regarding the proposal. She 
also requested additional information regarding traffic enforceme nt and accident statistics. Administration 
responded by noting ODOT's outreach efforts to businesses and property owners and encouraged residents 
to continue participating in City discussions. 
Communication s r ead by Mrs. Eadicicco : 
• From Jennifer D ick regarding Harvest Lane traffic concerns. The communication expressed concerns about 
speeding, speed bump placement, possible speed - limit reductions, neighborhood traffic safety, and 
opposition to the Reading Road R oad diet proposal. A response from Safety Service Director Ross was 
summarized, explaining speed bump placement standards and discussing possible future speed - limit reviews 
and signage options. 
• From David Rodenberg expressing opposition to the proposed Reading Road R oad diet and encouraging 
Council to reject the project. 
• From Kathy Healy expressing opposition to the road diet proposal and encouraging increased traffic 
enforcement as an alternative safety measure. 
Guest Speakers 
No guest speakers. 
E xecutive Sessio n 
No e xecutive session .

Page 3 07 - 0 7 - 202 6 Reading Council Minutes 
Administrative Reports 
Mayor's Report : Mayor Be mmes 
o A citywide newsletter was recently mailed to approximately 5,200 residences. 
o The Water Utility Department has begun implementing electronic billing while retaining traditional 
payment methods. 
o Residents were advised of upcoming Interstate 75 northbound closures and expected traffic impacts. 
o The Ohio EPA advised that no environmental issues were found at the former Givaudan site and that 
suspension of development resulted from business decisions rather than environmental conditions. 
o Administration requested Council approval of the 2027 Budget Ordinance in order to meet county filing 
deadlines. 
Law Director's Report : Mr. Stevenson 
• No business. 
Treasurer's Report : Treasurer Owens 
• June income tax collections totaled approximately $752,406. 
• Year - to - date collections totaled approximately $5.04 million. 
• Collections are currently approximately 4.6% below the same period in 2025, although comparable to prior 
ye a r s . 
Council Committee Reports 
Finance Committee 
• Mr. Bronner reported that the committee reviewed the proposed 2027 budget and recommended its 
advancement to Council. Fund consolidation options were also discussed. 
Utilities, Lands and Buildings Committee 
• Mr. Bishop reported on discussions regarding the Reconnecting Communities and Neighborhoods project, 
with a presentation scheduled for a future meeting. 
Zoning, Planning and Environment Committee 
• Mr. Powell announced a committee meeting July 21,2026 at 6 :30 pm to review Planning Commission 
recommendations related to proposed zoning changes. 
Laws and Contracts Committee 
• Mrs. E adicicco reported on discussions concerning possible expansion of Community Reinvestment Areas 
(CRA) and future grant - writing opportunities. 
Public Health and Safety

Page 4 07 - 0 7 - 202 6 Reading Council Minutes 
• Mayor Bemmes , reporting in the absence of Mrs. Kro e ger, summarized June Police and Fire Department 
activity: 
o 1,015 police calls for service , 28 vehicle accidents , 147 citations issued. 
o 213 EMS responses , 51 fire responses. 
o Additional updates included traffic enforcement efforts, hydrant maintenance, and staffing challenges 
related to firefighter recruitment and retention. 
Service Committee 
• Mr. B oe hner reviewed numerous public works activities, including: 
o Street and sidewalk repairs , w ater - main repairs , c atch basin work , c rosswalk and pavement markings , 
s treet sweeping , p ark and facility maintenance and i nstallation of fencing at Koenig Park. 
• Mr s. Eadicicco mentioned that the Civil Service testing for Police Officer positions will be held July 25, 2026, 
to fill four vacancies. National Night Out will be held August 4 at Koenig Park. 
• Chairm an Mr. Boehner announced committee mee tin g on July 21, 2026 at 6:30 pm. 
Recreation Committee 
• Mr. T ham ann reported progress on the new dog park, including grading completion and upcoming fence 
installation. Pool memberships currently total 592 memberships representing approximately 2,342 
individual members. 
• Council referred the topic of accessibility improvements at Koenig Park and ADA curb - cut improvements to 
the recreation committee for discussion. Motion by Mr. Br onner, second by Mr s. Eadicicco. Motion carried 
by voice vote. 
Legislative Session 
Resolution – A R ESOLUTION SUPPORTING OHIO DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION ’ S READING ROAD (U .S. 42) 
ROAD DIET. 
• Council conducted the first reading of a resolution supporting ODOT's proposed Reading Road (U.S. 42) Road 
Diet project. 
• Members expressed differing viewpoints regarding public opinion, safety concerns, pedestrian 
improvements, traffic impacts, and possible alternatives. No vote was taken, and declared a first reading 
Ordinance – A N ORDINANCE AUTHORIZING COMPENSATION TO BRYAN EDENS FOR ACC RUED SICK TIME . 
• Mr . Boe h ner made a motion to suspend the rules requiring a third reading , se cond by Mr. Bronner to adopt 
an ordinance authorizing compensation to Brian Edens for accrued sick and vacation leave. Motion carried 
after a 6 - 0 roll call vote. Motion to ado pt by Mr. Boehner, second by Mr s. Eadicicco . Motion carried after a 
6 - 0 roll call vote. Ordinance No. 2026 - 19. 
Ordinance – T HE F OLLOWING BUDGET FOR THE CALENDAR Y EAR BEGINNING JANURARY 1, 2027 HAS BEEN 
ADOPTED BY COUNCIL AND IS HEREBY SUBMITTED FOR CONSIDERATION OF THE HAMILTON COUNT Y BUDGEG 
COMMISSION.

Page 5 07 - 0 7 - 202 6 Reading Council Minutes 
• Mr s. Eadicicco ma de a motion to suspend the rules requiring a third reading , second by Mr. Bronner . Motion 
carried after a 6 - 0 roll call vote. Motion by Mr. Boehner, second by Mr. Bronner to adopt the ordinance 
approving and submitting the 2027 budget to the Hamilton County Budget Commission. Moti on carr ied by a 
6 - 0 roll call vote. Ordinance No. 2026 - 20 . 
Ordinance – AN ORDINANCE AUTHORIZING THE SAFETY SERVICE DIRECTOR TO PURCHASE PERSONAL PR OTECTIVE 
EQUIPMENT FOR THE FIRE DEPARTMENT . 
• Mr . Boe hner ma de a motion to suspend the rules requiring a third reading , second by Mr. B ishop . Motion 
carried by a 6 - 0 rol L call vote. Motion by Mr. Bronner, second by Mrs. Eadic icco to adopt an ordinance 
authorizing the purchase of personal protective equipment for the Fire Department. Motion carried by a 6 - 0 
roll call vote. Ordinance No. 2026 - 21 . 
Miscellaneous Business 
• Planning has begun for the 2026 Holiday Walk and volunteers are being sought. 
• Mayor Bemmes expressed appreciation for former officer Brian Edens and recognized his 26 years of service 
to the City of Reading. 
Adjournment 
Motion to adjourn by Mr . Boehner , seconded by Mr. Thamann , carried by 6 - 0 voice vote. Adjourned at 9: 10 pm.
